CB30: Crooks & Scams

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We show the range of trickery that consumers have been exposed to and the confrontations on behalf of victims.

Unique Selling Point:
30 years of crooks and conmen have met their sticky end on Carte Blanche. Join us for some epic confrontations - and a variety of reactions worthy of the five stages of grief: denial, anger, bargaining, depression and acceptance.

Script:


CROOKS & SCAMS


Bongani: It’s us from Carte Blanche. And we’ve caught you at it again, we’d like to talk to you.

V/O: It’s been described as a nightmare come true – a Carte Blanche crew on your doorstep demanding answers.

Coetzee: Close the front door, quick!

Ruda: Okay we heard that. Could we speak to Mr Coetzee please?

Coetzee: Close the front door!

Ruda: Clearly, he didn’t want to speak to us.

V/O: For three decades we’ve been the scourge of scamsters and crooks.

Maggie: What do you want?

Devi: Maggie! Can we speak to you?

Maggie: No, you cannot!

Devi: It’s your right to reply, you have the opportunity to do that.

Maggie: Close the fucking door. Go! Jissis! Close the fucking door!

Devi: Why did you go into hiding on Tuesday?

Gilbert: Because I was running away from you.

V/O: You can run, but you can’t hide – as this booking agent discovered after accepting payment for strippers who no longer strip.

Devi: Hello Paulo!

Paulo: How you doing?

Devi: Devi, Carte Blanche, how are you? No don’t head for the door because I want to talk to you. Oh are you leaving? Oh, then I’m just going to run behind you then. Your pants are falling down, why don’t you pull them up?

V/O: But even when we do pin them down, they still manage to duck and dive.

Bongani: Did you take his money or not?

Francois: At, at, at, at, at, at that point in time I didn’t take his money. So I will duly respond with my attorney, I’m not going to continue the interview.

V/O: When confronted with their misdemeanors, most crooks seems to go through the Five Stages of Grief, starting with Denial.

Text: Denial

PI: Last week you’ve been receiving stolen property - chocolates and Halls

Mr Pereira: Stolen stuff?

PI: That’s right, ja.

Mr Pereira: Where is it? Can’t I buy stuff in Checkers if I want to?

PI: Okay bring me the invoices for this please?

Mr Pereira: Oh I can’t have it.

V/O: And armed response guards caught stealing jewelry and booze in this house denied it – even when shown the footage.

Guard 1: It is not me there.

Les: But then he changed his mind.

Guard 1: It was me there, but I didn’t take anything.

Guard 2: I checked the booze there, lying down the floor there, and then leave it there and go out.

Les: You didn’t take a bottle?

Guard 2: No.

V/O: But fridge-raiding hungry Jannie, also turned out to be a bit of a joker.

Jannie: I didn’t really raid the fridge. If I raided, how can I say, there will be nothing there.

V/O: And then there was the Women’s World Cup of Golf.

Devi: Staff members were instructed to take sign from streets and replace the signs with Project Golf branding.
Have you ever taken Sotheby’s signboards to put your own signage in it?

Tania: Ha, ha, ha, ha – I have not, no.

V/O: We also put some Durban electricians to the test, and they failed miserably.

Bongani: You’ve told them specifically they need a new Distribution Board?

Electrician: No. no.

Bongani: But we’ve recorded his earlier visit.

Electrician: You need a new DB box.

Nicci: Oh, do I? Ok.

Bongani: Can I tell you what the problem is? It’s the stove.

Electrician: It’s the stove? I thought so.

V/O: And while in Durban we visited Schabir Shaik, awaiting his fraud and corruption trial.

Schabir: So I think it’s a pipe dream for anyone to suggest that just knowing Deputy-President Zuma opens up a whole host of business opportunities.

V/O: The Judge disagreed – and so would the Guptas.

Devi: Italian brand Pinarello is regarded as the Ferrari of bicycles.

V/O: But Cycle Science in Joburg was selling fakes, at full price.

Devi: Why are you selling fakes?

John: We don’t, even stock them. They request it from us.

Devi: But why did you say yes, I’ll do it? Why are you even dealing with fake anything?

Robbie: Some people want the look alike, but they can’t afford to pay the price.

V/O: And then there was the Rustenburg Copper King buying stolen copper.

Chantal: Do you own the cash for scrap shops?

King: Not anymore.

Chantal: You don’t?

King: No, I’m finished.

Chantal: Funny that, just minutes earlier he owned a couple.

King: Yes, I have the most. I have eleven.

Chantal: Do you buy from people who come off the street?

King: No.

Chantal: Are you still dealing with all the cash for the streets?

King: No.

V/O: Private school Arvanites College employed unqualified teachers, gave out answers during exams, and faked matric certificates.

Sheryl: I don’t believe those results are fraudulent.

Bongani: This is the real document. Some of these results do not match.

Sheryl: I understand that some of these results do not match, but I don’t have, I don’t know how these results, where they came from, who did what with them, I have no idea.

Bongani: You made this up, didn’t you?

Sheryl: No, why would I do that?

V/O: And online romance turned into a heartbreak hustle.

Chantal: Are you at all involved in an online dating scam?

David: No, I have never.

Chantal: Fleecing women for their money?

David: No, no never. Enough is enough, before I broke your camera. I have spoken to you, I am done with you.

Man 2: Just get out from our face, and don’t, don’t, don’t, don’t show us any camera here.

V/O: The next stage is inevitably Anger. Like the time we exposed diesel skimming, when diesel was R3.00 a litre.

Text: Anger

Mr Nel: Take one more photo from me. You’re taking from the wrong person photos, China. I take you to fucking Court.

V/O: Then there was the Rand Flight Academy who were selling pilot’s licenses to Nigerians.

Tas: Bribes! I kill you rather than take a bribe. I want to know who’s the son of a bitch who spreads rumours like this. I will kill him!

Derek: I don’t think I’ve seen anything this quite disgustingly dirty in my life.

V/O: Derek exposed the horrors of a Pretoria puppy mill.

Derek: Jan, how’s it going?

Jan: ja, bloody, very shit. No, don’t greet me, just fucking leave me alone.

V/O: A week later, not much had improved – including his mood.

Devi: But you can’t deny that the situation wasn’t great here?

Jan: No shut up now about it, I know it’s not right, but just keep quiet about it. I’m getting irritated.

Devi: Don’t tell me to shut up, I’m speaking to you so nicely Jan.

Jan: No, but you’re not speaking nicely to me.

Devi: I am speaking to you nicely.

Jan: You’re saying the same thing, like an Indian and a Black always say the same things over and over.

Devi: Oh you’re turning this into a racial issue now, don’t Jan.

Jan: No, I’m bringing racial things in.

V/O: And Pretoria’s rubble queen claimed to know nothing about her trucks dumping illegally.

Marietjie: Ok, where did you drop off that load?

Riaan: I’m going to shove that thing up your butt!

V/O: But threats turned to violence with Durban’s Gumtree Gang.

Pops: Get out!

Devi: The Gumtree Gang turned on the Carte Blanche Crew. (screams)

V/O: The attack left the Crew bleeding and the Gumtree Gang were convicted of assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm.

Text: Bargaining

But some crooks try to bargain their way out of a tight spot. Like the man who sold hundreds of dream holidays on a non-existent cruise ship.

Sam: A ship will arrive somewhere in January in Durban.

Devi: Where is it coming from and where will it go?

Sam: I can’t just speak on behalf of another company.

V/O: Because he had nothing to do with Starlight Cruises.

MSC: It’s the Rhapsody.

Devi: But that’s your ship?

MSC: Yes, that’s the only ship I think that will be here in January.

V/O: And car service stories always come with smooth talkers.

Phone: Listen, do you want to come up here I’ve got a bit of a problem. I’ve got… it’s Carte Blanche hey?

Ruda: Do you get a clear anti-freeze?

Guy 1: Um you get a yellow, and a pink, a red. And then here’s an anti-freeze here, a brand new one. It’s clear.

Ruda: But, isn’t distilled water always clear?

Guy 1: Ja its exactly like water, exactly. You know you do get monkeys out there. The motor industry has got a terrible name.

V/O: And there’s the fake homeopath who seemed disappointed to see us.

Zaa: Dr Grigorova.

Dr: Yes.

Zaa: Zaa from Carte Blanche.

Dr: Oh?

Zaa: Why are you practicing in South Africa without being registered?

Dr: No, I’m not registered but I work in the medical sphere and I pay my taxes.

V/O: This crooked couple were caught shaving thousands of kilometres off the odometers of various cars but tried to justify their actions.

Ruda: But it’s certainly illegal, and you know it?

Charlotte: Well we do repairs, so if they ask us, it’s not us that’s illegal.

V/O: There are those who developed amnesia – probably triggered by depression.

Ruda: R552 for an imaginary thermostat is a good profit margin for Amakhosi Plumbing.

Richard: Jissie Ruda, I can’t remember now, let me just see. Ruda to be honest, I can really not remember it. I really can’t remember, I wouldn’t do that. I always put a thermostat in. I can’t think, what does the house look like? I can’t really remember. Ruda, I really can’t remember. To be honest, I really can’t remember it.

V/O: And the finance woman at Planet Wheels lost her hearing when customers demanded payment for cars sold on consignment.

Riaan: They told me that she’s deaf and you won’t be able to talk to her.

Derek: Is Jenny deaf?

Lyn: She has a hearing problem yes.

Derek: But from what we saw and heard at Ocean’s Rest, Jenny has made a miraculous recovery.

Sharon: She’s definitely not deaf!

V/O: And finally, with the realization there’s no escape, comes acceptance.

Derek: Ahmed?

Ahmed: Yes sir.

Derek: Derek Watts.

Ahmed: How are you Derek?

Derek: From Carte Blanche.

Ahmed: I know you Sir.

Derek: I’m just helping a lady.

Derek: Well, we actually know what you’re doing. You’re actually slowing down meters all over town.

Ahmed: Start trying to make a living now.

V/O: From the municipal meter cheater, to the dodgy diesel engine dealer.

Malcolm: I do admit that some people were strung along. I don’t’ deny that, it’s a fact.

Ian: Because I wouldn’t even take a wheelbarrow to him. It would come back without a wheel.

V/O: To the treacherous transport broker…

Elsie: Ja, I ‘m guilty of that.

Devi: Are you charging VAT?

Elsie: Yes, I do.

Devi: Are you crazy?

Elsie: Yes.

Devi: That’s fraud?

Elsie: Ja, I know.

V/O: To the crooked mileage correction specialist….

Devi: We’ve got footage of you turning back the clocks on both those vehicles. So what do you have to say?

Louis: I’m guilty.

V/O: And when this sparky had talked himself into a corner, he simply bolted.

Bongani: Do you have it in the car maybe?

Ivan: Yes.

Bongani: So should I follow you to the car?

Ivan: Yes.

Bongani: Ivan had reached the stairwell. We followed him. He’s written it down somewhere. Wait, Mr Naidoo, I’m coming! Well he left his partner behind.

Partner: I can’t take all of this on the taxi.

Bongani: So, are you going now?

Partner: I can’t stand this.

Bongani: Ivan never came back, abandoning his assistant.
